small_guidance:
- The ConvTranspose2d dominates (~20ms); tuning the mean/finalize tail won't move the needle. If staying small, at minimum reduce mean kernel overhead: increase SPLIT to 16-32 with BLOCK=8192 and num_warps=8 to better saturate memory bandwidth on the 16×128×514×514 output tensor.
- Fuse the bias-add + mean into a single pass over the conv output (one program per (N, OC), striding HW with vectorized loads, num_warps=8, num_stages=3) to eliminate the partial buffer round-trip.
- Use channels_last (NHWC) layout on the conv output so the mean reduction over (H,W) is contiguous per channel and coalesces better.
large_guidance:
- Replace nn.ConvTranspose2d with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, input-spatial tile), computing input × weight outer product (kernel_size=3, so 9 output positions per input element) and scatter-adding into the (N, OC, H+2, W+2) grid. This is the heavy op (~20ms of 20.5ms total) and the only place with real headroom.
- Fuse the mean reduction directly into the conv-transpose epilogue: maintain per-(N, OC) running sums in a second kernel pass (or use atomics into an (N, OC) accumulator) so the full (N, OC, 514, 514) tensor is never written back to HBM — it's 16·128·514·514·4 ≈ 17 GB of traffic that currently dominates runtime.
- After the fused conv+mean produces (N, OC) means, run the existing tiny finalize kernel (bias + logsumexp + ×10) on that small tensor. Keep the conv accumulation loop iterating over the full (kh, kw, IC) work to respect the safety contract — do not pre-sum weights across kh,kw.
